verification_report.summary: The proof is correct relative to the explicitly supplied dependencies. The CLD-to-classical comparison extract is consistent with the curve test and decreasing-limit argument. Scalar descent is exactly [Gubler–Rabinoff, Proposition 7.2(6)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=35), with matching definitions and hypotheses. In the principal proposition, linearity gives zero Hessian currents for both signs after extension; the second gate then gives CLD-psh and hence classical pluriharmonicity. Scalar descent and the supplied singular theorem give classical pluriharmonicity and local real piecewise linearity on X. When X is pure-dimensional, the original current equation and the supplied real-PL comparison give semipositivity of both signs, hence GJR harmonicity. The corollary correctly negates the two-gate implication for each extension and specializes to L=K. Its final converse claim concerns the locally integrable scope of the forward CLD-to-positive-current implication, not the separately stated smooth converse. All deductions and dependency hypotheses pass; the stipulated long book arguments were not reverified.
